lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` route returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the root GET path
Server is up; open this URL

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
Path operation decorator for HTTP GET
Root path "/" calls the function
uvicorn main:app — file name and app name
--reload auto-restarts on file changes

hints: Install both packages first: pip install fastapi uvicorn.
In main.py, import FastAPI and create app = FastAPI(), then decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
Run uvicorn from the folder containing main.py: uvicorn main:app --reload.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in the browser; you should see {"Hello":"World"}.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi and getting 'uvicorn: command not found'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory, causing 'Could not import module "main"'.
Using main.py:app or a wrong app variable name in the uvicorn command.
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI(), so app is the class, not an instance.
Naming the file fastapi.py, which shadows the library import.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: In main.py create an empty `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. With uvicorn running, test it with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Empty in-memory list holding the items
POST endpoint on the /items path
item is read from the query string
Send a POST request with ?item=apple

explanations.topic: What routes are in FastAPI
A POST request to /items calls create_item
A plain str argument becomes a query parameter
Returning the whole list to see the results

hints: Above your routes, create an empty list named items. Then add a new function decorated with @app.post for the "/items" path.
The function takes one argument, item: str. FastAPI treats it as a query parameter, e.g. ?item=apple.
Inside the function, call items.append(item) and then return items. Keep uvicorn running (with --reload) so the change is picked up.
In a second terminal, run: curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'. It should print ["apple"].
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post. curl -X POST then returns {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}.
Leaving out ?item=... in the URL. This gives a 422 error saying the field is required.
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so the ? or & characters get interpreted by the shell.
Defining items = [] inside the function, which resets the list on every request.
Running curl in the same terminal as uvicorn, or forgetting to restart uvicorn when it was started without --reload.
Returning item instead of items (this is allowed, but then the output shows only the new item, not the list).

steps.title: Add GET endpoint by item ID
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. After adding items, curl /items/0 and /items/1 to retrieve them.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with item_id path parameter
Index the items list with the path variable

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly braces map URL segments to variables
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Path value becomes the function argument
Type hints let FastAPI convert the path value to int
Out-of-range index causes an internal server error

hints: The path goes in the decorator: /items/ followed by the variable name in curly braces.
The function argument must have the same name as the variable in the path, e.g. item_id.
Add the type hint `: int` so FastAPI converts "0" to the integer 0 before you index the list.
The server reloads on save and empties the list. POST a couple of items again before you curl /items/0.
common_mistakes: Function parameter name doesn't match the {item_id} placeholder, so FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Leaving out the `: int` type hint, so indexing the list with a string raises TypeError.
Testing GET right after saving without re-adding items. The reload reset the list, so you get a 500 error.
Requesting an index that doesn't exist (e.g. /items/3) and taking the 500 error as a bug in the route. The next step handles this case.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import `HTTPException` from fastapi and in get_item raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...)` when the index is out of range. Curl a missing index to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi
Raise a 404 with a helpful detail message
The curl response shows the 404 detail

explanations.topic: Why an unhandled error becomes an unhelpful 500 Internal Server Error
HTTP response status codes; missing items are a client error
404 Not Found is the right code for a missing item
The detail parameter adds a reason to the error response

hints: Before returning the item, check whether item_id is a valid index into your items list.
Import HTTPException alongside FastAPI: from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException.
In the else branch, use raise (not return) HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found").
Make sure uvicorn reloaded (run with --reload), then curl an index past the end of the list, e.g. /items/7.
common_mistakes: Using return HTTPException(...) instead of raise, which sends a 200 response rather than a 404.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError and still returns a 500.
Using <= len(items) in the condition, so the last+1 index still raises IndexError.
Testing with an index that exists, so the 404 never appears.
Not restarting or reloading uvicorn, so the old code still returns Internal Server Error.

steps.title: List items with limit query parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Test with `curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.

targets.caption: List endpoint taking an int limit query parameter
Slice the list to the first limit items
Call the endpoint with limit=3

explanations.topic: Path vs query parameters; create_item currently takes item as a query string
FastAPI converts query string values to the annotated type (int)
Same /items path, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value in the function signature is used when limit is omitted

hints: Add a new route with the same "/items" path as create_item, but use @app.get instead of @app.post.
Give the function a parameter `limit: int = 10`. Because it isn't in the path, FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return `items[0:limit]` to slice the list. Then POST a few items and run curl with `?limit=3`.
Full code: @app.get("/items")\ndef list_items(limit: int = 10):\n    return items[0:limit]
common_mistakes: Using @app.post on the new route, so GET /items returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Leaving out the `: int` annotation, so limit stays a string and slicing raises a TypeError (500 error).
Testing right after a server restart: the in-memory list is empty, so the result is [] until items are POSTed again.
Leaving the URL unquoted in the shell, so `?` or `&` gets interpreted by the shell.
Writing the path as "/items/" or "/item" so it doesn't match the curl URL (404 or redirect).

steps.title: Define Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: Import `BaseModel` from pydantic and define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, then use `item: Item` in create_item. POST JSON with `curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"apple"}' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items'`.

targets.caption: Pydantic Item model with text and is_done
create_item now takes an Item JSON body
Response is an object matching the model

explanations.topic: Why use Pydantic models: structure, validation, docs, IDE completion
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not query parameters
Default values: is_done defaults to false
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and subclass it to make an Item class with a text string and an is_done boolean.
Give is_done a default of False so clients don't have to send it.
Change create_item's parameter to item: Item, and annotate get_item to return Item.
The old curl with ?item=... won't work. Send JSON with -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"apple"}' and drop the query string.
common_mistakes: Reusing the old curl request with the item as a query parameter, which gets a 422 because the body is missing.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header on the curl POST.
Defining class Item without inheriting from BaseModel.
Using single quotes inside the JSON payload. JSON keys and strings need double quotes.
Removing the default on text and then sending a payload with a different key such as title, which fails validation.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: Add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Save and verify responses still return Item-shaped JSON.

targets.caption: Single item response model on get_item
List response model on list_items

explanations.topic: Using a Pydantic model for responses, not just requests
response_model argument in the route decorator
Defined response structure helps front-end clients like React/Next.js

hints: The change goes in the route decorators (@app.get(...)), not in the function bodies.
Add a keyword argument called response_model to each decorator.
For the single-item route use response_model=Item; for the list route use response_model=list[Item].
If the server didn't reload, re-run `uvicorn main:app --reload` and check for 'Application startup complete'.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model in the function signature instead of the decorator.
Using response_model=Item on the list endpoint, which makes FastAPI fail to validate a list response.
Writing list[Item] on Python < 3.9 instead of List[Item] from typing.
Defining the Item class below the routes so it is undefined when the decorator runs.
Misspelling the argument as response_models or responseModel.

steps.title: Explore interactive Swagger docs
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, use Try it out on POST /items and Execute. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click Try it out on POST /items, then Execute
The real response from your server appears here
Link to the raw OpenAPI schema

explanations.topic: FastAPI generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Execute shows the equivalent curl command and actually sends the request
/redoc is an alternative documentation view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses for building clients

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running in the terminal before opening the browser.
Go to http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs. Find POST /items, expand it and click 'Try it out'.
Edit the JSON request body so it matches your Item model, then click Execute and scroll down to the Response body.
Also try http://127.0.0.1:8000/redoc and http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json to see the generated schema.
common_mistakes: Server not running or stopped after an earlier error, so /docs won't load.
Forgetting to click 'Try it out', which leaves the request body read-only.
Sending a body that doesn't match the Pydantic Item model, which returns a 422 validation error.
Typing /doc or /docs/ with the wrong host or port instead of http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs.
